title: Data Protection & Secure Networking
oneLiner: Encrypt data everywhere and lock down the network with VPC controls, KMS, and edge protection.
examWeightNote: Completes Design Secure Architectures (30% of the exam).
objectives: Encrypt data at rest with KMS and in transit with TLS; know the difference between SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, and SSE-C.
Contrast security groups (stateful) with network ACLs (stateless).
Secure a VPC with subnets, route tables, NAT gateways, and VPC endpoints / PrivateLink.
Choose the right edge protection: AWS WAF, Shield, and when to add them to CloudFront/ALB.

services.name: AWS KMS
services.purpose: Managed keys for encrypting data at rest across S3, EBS, RDS, and more, with access controlled by IAM/key policies.

services.name: Security Groups
services.purpose: Stateful, instance-level virtual firewalls; return traffic is automatically allowed.

services.name: Network ACLs
services.purpose: Stateless, subnet-level allow/deny rules evaluated in order.

services.name: VPC Endpoints / PrivateLink
services.purpose: Reach AWS services (e.g. S3, DynamoDB) privately without traversing the internet.

services.name: AWS WAF & Shield
services.purpose: WAF filters HTTP(S) requests (SQLi, XSS, rate limits); Shield defends against DDoS.

keyConcepts: Security groups are stateful (allow inbound → return traffic is auto-allowed) and only support allow rules; NACLs are stateless and support both allow and deny.
SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys; SSE-KMS uses KMS keys (adds audit trail and key policies); SSE-C means you supply the key. For compliance/audit, SSE-KMS is common.
A gateway VPC endpoint (S3, DynamoDB) is free and uses route tables; interface endpoints (PrivateLink) create ENIs for most other services.
Place resources that shouldn't be internet-reachable in private subnets; use a NAT gateway for outbound-only internet access.
Attach AWS WAF to CloudFront, ALB, or API Gateway; AWS Shield Standard is automatic and free, Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS protection and cost protection.

scenarios.scenario: EC2 instances in a private subnet need to download objects from Amazon S3, but security policy forbids any route to the internet for these instances.
scenarios.question: How can the instances reach S3 privately?

options.label: Add a NAT gateway and route 0.0.0.0/0 to it
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3
Assign the instances public IP addresses

scenarios.explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps traffic on the AWS network with no internet route required — and it's free. A NAT gateway or public IPs would send traffic toward the internet, violating the policy.

scenarios.scenario: A public web app behind an Application Load Balancer is being hit with SQL-injection attempts and layer-7 request floods.
scenarios.question: Which service should you add to filter malicious HTTP requests?

options.label: AWS WAF with managed rule groups
A network ACL denying all traffic

scenarios.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests and can block SQLi/XSS and rate-limit floods when attached to CloudFront, ALB, or API Gateway. Inspector assesses vulnerabilities but doesn't filter live traffic.

quiz.question: Which statement about security groups is correct?
options: They are stateless and evaluated by rule number
They are stateful and support only allow rules
They operate at the subnet level
quiz.answer: They are stateful and support only allow rules
quiz.explanation: Security groups are stateful (return traffic is automatically allowed) and support allow rules only. NACLs are the stateless, subnet-level control that supports deny rules.

quiz.question: You need an audit trail of every use of the encryption key protecting an S3 bucket. Which option should you choose?
quiz.explanation: SSE-KMS uses AWS KMS keys, whose usage is logged in CloudTrail and controlled by key policies — ideal when you need auditing and fine-grained key control.

quiz.question: Which VPC endpoint type is used to privately access Amazon S3 and DynamoDB and is free of charge?
quiz.explanation: S3 and DynamoDB use gateway endpoints (route-table entries, no hourly charge). Most other services use interface endpoints (PrivateLink ENIs).

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a NAT gateway?
options: Allow inbound internet connections to private instances
Provide outbound-only internet access for instances in private subnets
Filter HTTP requests for SQL injection
quiz.answer: Provide outbound-only internet access for instances in private subnets
quiz.explanation: A NAT gateway lets private-subnet instances initiate outbound internet traffic (e.g. updates) while blocking unsolicited inbound connections.

quiz.question: AWS Shield Standard provides which of the following?
options: Automatic, no-cost protection against common network/transport-layer DDoS attacks
Web request filtering rules you configure
quiz.answer: Automatic, no-cost protection against common network/transport-layer DDoS attacks
quiz.explanation: Shield Standard is on by default at no extra cost for all AWS customers. Shield Advanced adds enhanced protections, 24/7 response, and cost protection for a fee.
